claims.text: Its stated purpose was early warning: 'to provide early warning of foreign scientific or technical advances, whether indigenous or imported, which could affect significantly the national security or national welfare of the United States.' Its initial substructure was three subcommittees, nine advisory groups and two working groups, including advisory groups on Behavioral and Human Engineering and on Lasers and Electro-optics.

claims.text: The committee was still operating in 1975 under a Letter of Instruction from the Deputy to the DCI for the Intelligence Community, which directed it to 'Complete the reorganization of the STIC and the transfer of subgroups to GMAIC during August 1975' and to coordinate all intelligence community activity on foreign science and technology that might lead to future threats to the US.

sources.name: CHARTER, STIC, 23 October 1974, and Letter of Instruction, 3 August 1975

desc: STIC was the United States Intelligence Board's standing committee on scientific and technical intelligence, renamed from the Scientific Intelligence Committee by a charter of 23 October 1974 to reflect a shift of emphasis toward technology. Its operating precept was early warning of foreign scientific or technical advances affecting national security, and it advised, and coordinated collection and production for, the USIB in those areas. Its charter lists among its Priority Group II objectives the assessment and establishment of an Intelligence Community position regarding certain unidentified foreign activities and anomalies in the science and technology area, which places a standing community mechanism for exactly that question inside the intelligence structure of the 1970s. A Letter of Instruction of 3 August 1975 shows the committee still operating under the Deputy to the DCI for the Intelligence Community and reorganising its subgroups.

timeline.text: The charter of the Scientific and Technical Intelligence Committee records the renaming from the Scientific Intelligence Committee and lists among its Priority Group II objectives the 'Assessment and establishment of an Intelligence Community position regarding certain unidentified foreign activities and anomalies in the S&T area'. The committee advises the United States Intelligence Board and coordinates collection and production in those areas. Nothing in the charter mentions the Robertson Panel.
